item.subject: maths
item.stem:
Kiran studies the diagram of triangles $ABC$ and $PQR$. Matching tick marks show $AB = PQ$, $BC = QR$, and $CA = RP$.

Which claim correctly decides congruence from those side lengths?

options.A: The three matching side lengths are enough: triangles $ABC$ and $PQR$ are congruent by SSS.
options.B: The triangles are congruent because each figure is labelled with three letters.
options.C: Congruence here also needs a right angle before the side lengths can be used.
options.D: The congruence name is decided first, and only afterwards do the matching side lengths matter.
